claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is in an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
Bulk arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons of this alloy typically exhibit the ordered single-phase hexagonal state.
Oblique-angle sputter deposition can produce a nanocolumnar or porous FeMnNiGeSi film while retaining its primary hexagonal phase.
Composition must be controlled to distinguish processing-induced microstructural effects from compositional effects on magnetic behavior.
A nanocolumnar or porous microarchitecture increases the alloy film's effective surface-to-volume ratio.
Increasing the surface-to-volume ratio facilitates more rapid heat exchange during the magnetostructural transition.
The nanostructured architecture increases the rate of thermal equilibration.
Faster thermal equilibration reduces localized thermal gradients during the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Reduced thermal gradients and diminished latent-heat bottlenecks decrease hysteresis.
Nanostructuring can reduce hysteresis without substantially decreasing the magnetocaloric entropy change.
Relative to conventional bulk forms, nanostructured films will retain a similarly large magnetocaloric effect.
Relative to conventional bulk forms, nanostructured films will exhibit significantly reduced hysteretic losses.
Relative to conventional bulk forms, nanostructured films will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric transition profile.
A broader transition profile and lower hysteretic losses will enable more efficient magnetic-refrigeration cycles.
Conventional bulk FeMnNiGeSi forms have limited surface-to-volume ratios and display a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
The predicted behavior requires preservation of the ordered hexagonal phase under low applied magnetic fields.
Extreme processing conditions or processing-induced phase changes may produce unwanted microstructural instabilities and invalidate the predictions.
The magnitude of hysteresis reduction and transition broadening depends on nanostructural parameters such as column diameter, spacing, and connectivity.
Dense sputtered films provide a control for nanocolumnar or porous films when composition and phase are held constant.
Failure to improve both heat-exchange rate and hysteresis, or a notable loss of magnetocaloric entropy change, would falsify the proposed nanostructuring mechanism.

contradictions.description: The stated initial material is an as-deposited alloy but is characterized as typical of arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons. The prediction then uses bulk forms as the comparator, whereas the falsification experiment uses a dense sputtered film as the control, leaving the operative baseline inconsistent.
